History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
23-year-old female with a 3–4-day history of constant, worsening midline lower-abdominal pain (8/10) accompanied by light vaginal bleeding and intermittent nausea, evaluated via teleconsultation; face-to-face assessment and same-day pregnancy test arranged.

History:
• Chief complaint: Constant lower-abdominal pain, midline below the umbilicus.  
• Onset/duration: Began “a few days ago,” progressively worsening.  
• Severity: 8/10.  
• Character: Present continuously; episodes become “very bad.”  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: None specified.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Light pink vaginal bleeding since after LMP (period ended ~2 weeks ago).  
  – Nausea without vomiting.  
  – Constipation for one week last week; bowel habit now normal, stool not diarrheal.  
  – Mild clear/“small extra” vaginal discharge.  
  – Denies fever, chills, dyspnea, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness/syncope, dysuria, urinary frequency/urgency, hematuria, diarrhea, weight loss, or blood per rectum/urine.  
• Last menstrual period: ~2–3 weeks ago; described as normal. Cycles irregular since starting contraceptive implant one year ago.  
• Sexual history: Sexually active; last intercourse 4 days ago; uses etonogestrel implant (inserted ~1 year ago).  
• Pregnancy history: G0. Home pregnancy test negative ~1 month ago; none since pain onset.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No prior surgeries.  
• No prior pregnancies.

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• No other regular medications reported.

Allergies:
• Amoxicillin – allergy (reaction type not specified).

Social History:
• Occupation: School teacher.  
• Living situation: Resides with husband and husband’s family.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Denies use.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.  
• Recent travel: Abroad one year ago; none recently.

Family History:
• Not discussed / none documented.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed – teleconsultation; patient to attend clinic for abdominal examination.

Investigations:
• Home urine pregnancy test negative one month ago (pre-symptom onset).  
• Plan for repeat pregnancy test today (result pending).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute worsening lower-abdominal pain with light vaginal bleeding.  
  • Differential includes early intra-uterine pregnancy or ectopic pregnancy, pelvic inflammatory disease, ovarian/gynecologic pathology, gastrointestinal causes (e.g., constipation).  
  • Plan:  
    – Arrange urgent face-to-face clinic visit for abdominal and, if indicated, pelvic examination.  
    – Repeat urine pregnancy test today; patient instructed to call immediately if positive.  
    – Safety-net: Advise emergency care if pain intensifies, new fever, inability to keep fluids down, syncope, shoulder pain, heavy bleeding, or positive pregnancy test.

Issue 2: Recent constipation (resolved).  
  • No active management required at present; review digestion/ bowel habits at in-person visit.

General Plan items:  
• Review allergy details and full medication list at next encounter.  
• Document vitals and perform full abdominal and pelvic exam in clinic.  
• Consider pelvic ultrasound and relevant labs (CBC, CRP, β-hCG) after examination.  
• Follow-up: Face-to-face appointment to be booked via support line; earlier if red-flag symptoms occur.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing/expected elements: No vitals taken; no physical exam; no full medication reconciliation; reaction details for amoxicillin allergy missing.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional incomplete sentences and minor audio gaps but clinically adequate.
